messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: ZIgzag sampling
parts:
Rowan:

Before you address the specific type of sampling design (type of zigzag
pattern to employ), you need to to contemplate some more considerable
matters. If your study organisms mainly inhabit an area 3km x 0.2km,
then you have a study area that is comprised largely of 'edge.' But the
idea that you might have unequal coverage probabilities is less of a
concern than your ability to get sufficient effort within that study
area to have enough detections to do a good job of estimation.

If truncation distance (distance at which animals are detectable) is
200m from the line, you could place 15 parallel lines each of 200m
length running perpendicular to your bush/pasture boundary. Assess what
sort of encounter rate you are likely to have with these animals, then
ask of 3km of sampling effort is adequate to perform estimation with
your desired degree of precision (see section 7.2.2 of Buckland et al.
(2001)).

If you come to a positive conclusion on that issue, then you can move on
to contemplate whether to use a zigzag sampler.
